clue.text: Running commercial vehicles on initially tight allowance

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, shortened to ad
Minis are small cars

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word tight

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies

explanation.surface: A haulage firm's lorries running on a very tight allowance of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like part of the picture, but it is the definition, as in running a company. 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a business means managing it, and management is what this word describes.

clue.text: Praise a Conservative allegation

parts.note: a claim is an assertion or allegation

explanation.surface: A political smear: a Tory's allegation passed off as praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean enthusiastic public approval, as a noun or a verb.

clue.text: What bridegroom may get me at rip-roaring resorts bordering Oman's capital

indicators.note: bordering means the scrambled letters sit on either side of the capital letter of Oman
resorts is read as re-sorts, so the letters before it are sorted into a new order
capital means the first letter of the word Oman's

explanation.surface: A holiday tale of wild nights in seaside resorts around the Gulf of Oman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorts' looks like holiday places but signals re-sorting ME AT RIP ROARING, which is then split around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowry, money or property brought by the bride, is what the groom might receive on marrying.

clue.text: One dubious name for inert gas

indicators.note: dubious means doubtful or shaky, so the letters of One are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone casts doubt on a name proposed for a noble gas.
explanation.definitionFit: This element is one of the noble gases, chemically unreactive, hence inert.

clue.text: Individual in sleeveless vest, taking time off

indicators.note: taking with off tells us a letter is to be removed from the vest
off completes taking off, removing the time letter

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest worn by athletes or as underwear

explanation.surface: Someone in a sleeveless vest takes time off from work.
explanation.definitionFit: Single and individual both mean one alone, separate from others.

clue.text: True about victim being in denial

indicators.note: about means the word for true goes round the word for victim

parts.note: real means genuine or true
a butt is the target or victim of jokes

explanation.surface: It is true that the victim is in denial about what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a contradiction or refutation, a formal denial of a claim.

clue.text: Rookie in bid to join infantry

indicators.note: to join means the two pieces are joined side by side

parts.note: a tender is a formal bid for a contract
foot soldiers are the infantry

explanation.surface: A new recruit tries to sign up for the infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderfoot is a newcomer or novice, inexperienced like a rookie.

clue.text: Canteen had soups requiring stirring –- a matter easily resolved

indicators.note: stirring means the letters of the canteen phrase are mixed up like a pot of soup

explanation.surface: A canteen with soups that needed stirring: a trivial problem quickly sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring' is a link word between fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A case so clear it can be decided at once is an obvious, quickly settled matter.

clue.text: A grand on top

parts.note: swell is an old slang word for grand or excellent

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds extra, on top of everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A grand' looks like a thousand pounds, but grand is swell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean in addition, besides or additionally.

clue.text: Comic strip duck in tub

indicators.note: in means the zero goes inside the container

parts.note: a carton is a container, such as a tub of yoghurt
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A comic strip showing a duck sitting in a bathtub.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of drawn panels in a newspaper is a kind of cartoon.

clue.text: Prohibits importing German sausages

indicators.note: importing means bringing the German abbreviation into the word for prohibits

parts.note: bans means prohibits

explanation.surface: A trade ban on bringing in German sausages.
explanation.walkthrough: BANGERS is British slang for sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangers is British slang for sausages, from the way they burst when fried.

clue.text: Earnest opera singer making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means the singer's word is turned back to front

parts.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer

explanation.surface: An opera singer earnestly returning to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen and eager, close in sense to earnest or zealous.

clue.text: Nevertheless halt sale, silly me!

indicators.note: silly means the letters around it are treated foolishly and jumbled

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper scolds themself for stopping a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' reworks only HALT SALE; ME stays as written at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means however or even so, an equivalent of nevertheless.

clue.text: Shrewd setter is, we suspect

indicators.note: suspect means the words are dubious, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Solvers suspect the crossword setter is a shrewd one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worldly-wise in urban life means sharp and shrewd.

clue.text: Very great number heading off after start of migration

indicators.note: after means the trimmed number comes after that opening letter
start of means the opening letter of migration
heading off means the first letter is removed from the number

parts.note: eighty is a number

explanation.surface: A very great number of birds set off at the start of migration.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty means huge or immensely great in size or power.

clue.text: Recalled top of fancy flower

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the whole run of pieces is written backwards

parts.note: a lid is a top for a container
a fad is a passing fancy or craze

explanation.surface: Someone remembers the best of a fancy flower show.
explanation.walkthrough: LIDOFFAD read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The daffodil is a yellow spring flower of the narcissus family.

clue.text: Mythological king you almost sussed out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order
almost means the word you loses its final letter

explanation.surface: You almost worked out which mythological king it was.
explanation.walkthrough: YO plus SUSSED, rearranged. 'Sussed out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of the Odyssey was king of Ithaca in Greek myth.

clue.text: Pedlar is upset, sees what you're saying

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A street pedlar is upset, seeing what you are saying about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows speech by watching mouth movements literally sees what is being said.

clue.text: Added to register, the Queen's surgeon

indicators.note: added to means the royal letters are attached to the end of the register

parts.note: a list is a register or roll
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A royal surgeon is entered on the register.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister was the British surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister, pioneer of antiseptic surgery, is a famous surgeon.

clue.text: Again docked across the dam

indicators.note: across means the shortened word stretches across the word the
docked means cut short, losing its tail

parts.note: more means again, as in once more

explanation.surface: A boat docked again across from the dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' looks like a barrier on a river, but it is a female parent animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is the female parent of an animal, especially a horse.

clue.text: Direct punk trio to go on the rampage

parts.note: to run something is to direct or manage it

indicators.note: punk means rubbish or rotten, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone manages a punk trio that wrecks things on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is to behave wildly and violently, rampaging.

clue.text: Lynn, perhaps, banking on Italian city

indicators.note: banking means forming banks on either side, so the name goes round on

parts.note: Vera Lynn was the famous British wartime singer, so Lynn is a surname for Vera

explanation.surface: A singer called Lynn is banking on an Italian city tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Vera Lynn was the Second World War 'Forces' Sweetheart'. 'Lynn, perhaps' asks for someone whose surname is Lynn.
explanation.definitionFit: Verona is a city in northern Italy, setting of Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Dance waving pretty sash

indicators.note: waving means the letters flutter about into a new order

explanation.surface: A dancer waves a pretty sash.
explanation.walkthrough: A strathspey is a slow Scottish country dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The strathspey is a Scottish dance, slower than a reel.

clue.text: Enthusiasts returned in shock

indicators.note: returned means the word is sent back the other way

parts.note: nuts are fanatics or enthusiasts, as in health nuts

explanation.surface: Fans returned home in a state of shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'shock' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or astonish them.

clue.text: Cover skin

definitions.meaning: to cover something is to conceal it

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means conceal; as a noun, an animal pelt.

clue.text: Building equations, at first provided in numbered cubes

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of equations is used
in means the word for provided goes inside the cubes

parts.note: dice are cubes with numbered spots
if means provided, as in provided that

explanation.surface: A maths lesson: equations written on numbered cubes.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing building.

clue.text: Ring French friend about fake Japanese art

indicators.note: about places the French friend next to the word for fake, round the end of the ring

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O
to rig is to fix or fake, as in rigging an election
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: Phoning a French friend about some fake Japanese art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a verb, as in making a phone call, but it supplies the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese art of paper folding.

clue.text: A somewhat restrained comment below formal declaration

parts.note: under means below
a statement is a formal declaration

explanation.surface: A low-key remark tucked beneath an official announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: An understatement plays something down, a deliberately muted remark.
